newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Simeon board meets after Austvin bid rumour.
newsitem.headline: Simeon board meets after Austvin bid rumour.

text.p: Simeon Wines Ltd said on Tuesday its board of directors would meet today in response to speculation it will launch a takeover bid for fellow wine producer Australian Vintage Ltd.
But Simeon Wines would not comment on whether a bid could be launched.

"I am calling a directors' meeting today and we will make a press (statement) tomorrow to make our intentions one way or the other perfectly clear," Simeon managing director Neil MacKenzie told Reuters.

"We read all the speculation and innuendo in the press, we see Austvin has suspended their shares but the Simeon board of directors has not met to discuss any merger or acquisition of Austvin," he said.
Asked if Simeon would consider a bid at its meeting today, he said: "We will meet (today) to consider the press speculation about the bid."
Austvin on Monday requested its shares be suspended pending confirmation of whether or not a takeover bid would be received and newspaper reports have named Simeon as the likely source.
Simeon shares closed one cent lower at A$2.81 on Monday, while Austvin shares last closed at A$2.85 on Friday, giving the company a market capitalisation of A$105.2 million.

MacKenzie said it would be totally inappropriate for him to confirm or deny whether a bid could be launched, but added a merger of the two companies would be sensible as the businesses were very similar.
